prerequisites: Basic mathematics, and in particular drawing subsets of the plane described through equations/inequalities, and solving systems of equations.
Real analysis for one-variable functions (differential calculus, limits, integral calculus).
Basic linear algebra (vectors, analytic geometry in the plane and in the space, matrices, quadratic forms).

learning_outcomes.text: By the end of the course, the student must be familiar with and able to use the tools of multivariable analysis.
Solve exercises on the study of functions in several variables.
Solve optimization problems in several variables.
Calculate integrals on curves and surfaces.
Calculate the work of a vector field along a curve and the flux through a surface.
Develop critical thinking towards the basic notion of differential and integral calculus in several variables.
Be able to tackle and solve simple problems in an independent way.

syllabus_topics: Differential calculus for scalar functions of several variables: continuity, partial and directional derivatives, gradient, Hessian matrix, first- and second-order Taylor formulas.

Identification of critical points of a function and constrained critical points (via Lagrange multipliers); study of critical points via the Hessian matrix, identification of maximum and minimum points.
Partial derivatives and gradients of vector functions.
Integrals of several variables: definition and calculation methods; change-of-variable formula; volume of solids and of solids of revolution, differentiation of integrals.
Curves in the plane and in space: parameterizations, tangent line and tangent unit vector, length, integral of a function along a curve, work of a vector field along a curve.
Surfaces in space: parameterizations, tangent plane and normal vector, area, area of surfaces of revolution, integral of a function on a surface, flux of a vector field through a surface.
Gauss-Green theorem, divergence theorem, Stokes' theorem.

assessment_methods.method: Written test (second part: problems requiring detailed solutions)

assessment_rules: The exam consists primarily of a written test divided into two parts: the first requires only an answer (1 hour), and the second involves two or three problems with detailed solutions (2 hours). In some cases, an oral exam is also required. Knowledge acquisition will be assessed with exercises in a written exam and direct questions during an oral exam. Skills acquisition will be assessed with exercises and specific questions during the exam.
